**What broke:** Ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB. With the 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped, and the change went to all pods at once [1]. Dashboards were stale from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC on Nov 12. The rollback to v2.13.3 happened at 10:05, and lag fully drained at 12:27 [1][4].

**Data loss:** No. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late [1]. Lior's reconciliation matched event counts per workspace to the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [4]. Orbitly was told the same: all events were received and processed late, none lost [3].

**What we're changing:**
- ingest#419 reverts the default to 1 MB, adds a batcher guard that refuses batches over 25% of the container memory limit, and keeps 10 MB only for bulk import via explicit config [9].
- KES-431: page on-call when ingest consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes, due Nov 20 [11].
- KES-432: send ingest config changes to the canary pool first, owner Daniel, due Nov 27 [1].
- KES-433: raise the worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes, owner Lior, due Nov 27 [1].

The detection gap was the main problem: there was no consumer-lag alert, and the first signal was an OOM alert 27 minutes after the deploy [1].

Customer-facing follow-up: Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit under section 7 of their MSA [3][8]. Sam has told them he'll come back once finance has checked the terms [3]. The custom MSA isn't attached to the HubSpot deal, so Maya suggested asking Avi [8].
